lore.text: Born to the royal family of the planet Tamaran, Princess Koriand'r was the second oldest after her sister Komand'r. Because a childhood illness robbed Komand'r of her natural ability to use ultraviolet energy to fly, she was removed from the line of succession to the throne. Bitter, she fled to the enemy empire of the Citadel and gave them state secrets that enabled them to successfully invade Tamaran. The peace terms included Koriand'r being enslaved by the Citadel to ensure Tamaran's obedience. After six years of torture and abuse, Koriand'r was captured along with Komand'r by the Psions, aliens who experimented on them to see how much ultraviolet energy their bodies could absorb before dying. Instead, they gained the power to fire energy bolts and escaped. Koriand'r fled to Earth.

Pursued to Earth by the Citadel, Koriand'r was saved by the Teen Titans, a team of heroes united by Raven who was seeking help against her demonic father. With the ability to absorb languages by touch, Koriand'r found companionship, friendship, and adventure with the Titans, taking the heroic name Starfire. Adopting the Earth name Kory Anders, she began a career as a model. She dated and fell in love with a human man, but he was a spy working for the criminal organization, the H.I.V.E., which the Titans had defeated several times. However, he truly fell in love with Kori and was killed by the H.I.V.E. for refusing to betray her. The Titans brought his killers to justice. Later, Kori fell in love with her teammate Robin (Dick Grayson), a relationship that would prove enduring.

Dick and Kori stayed together as he became the team leader and changed his heroic identity to Nightwing. Their relationship was tested when Starfire brought him to her homeworld, which had won freedom from the Citadel. Her parents asked Kori to accept a marriage of state to Prince Karras to strengthen their planetary alliance against external enemies. It was for strategic purposes only, as Karras was in love with another and Kori did not love him. Kori agreed and didn't understand why Dick was so upset; on Tamaran, multiple spouses were not uncommon. Then when she had second thoughts, Dick refused to disrupt the wedding and harm her homeworld. In the end, a coup from Kori's sister Blackfire conquered Tamaran. Dick returned to Earth, while Kori and Karras stayed to mount a resistance.

Kori and Karras's resistance ultimately defeated Blackfire, but by that time, she had proved to be an effective ruler. Her parents agreed to share the throne with her, and Kori gave her blessing. She also gave her blessing for Karras to be with the woman he loved. Then she returned to Earth and the Titans. It took time, but eventually she and Nightwing got back together as well, and when they returned to Tamaran, it was on much better terms. Tragically, on that trip, Karras was killed saving Tamaran from a terrorist attack led by his long-lost sister. Later, Nightwing and Starfire almost married, but their wedding was disrupted by Raven, possessed by her demonic side. Afterward, shaken by the incident, they both realized they had things to figure out and went their separate ways.

Starfire, Blackfire, and several Titans (not including Nightwing) returned to Tamaran to fight an invasion by the Citadel, Psions, and Gordanians. Tamaranean General Ph'yzzon was captured and subjected to Psion experiments that gave him powers; Starfire rescued him. They bonded over their similar ordeals and later fell in love and married. When the war went badly, Ph'yzzon ordered a planetary evacuation. Starfire's parents remained on Tamaran and died when their planet was destroyed. It turned out the enemies of Tamaran were allied with the demonic Raven. When the Titans freed her from her father's influence, the alliance crumbled, and the Tamaraneans won the war, settling on a planet they called New Tamaran. Sadly, New Tamaran was later consumed by a Sun-Eater, and Ph'yzzon died defending it.

Many Tamaraneans survived, including Blackfire and her and Kori's brother, Ryand'r. Blaming the Gordanians for the destruction of Tamaran, they invaded their homeworld. The Titans helped negotiate a peace where the two people would share the world. Later, that planet was destroyed by Imperiex. Now the Tamaraneans wander the universe led by Blackfire. Starfire, who has accepted Earth as her home, and other teammates from the Titans, including Beast Boy, Nightwing, Cyborg, and Raven, formed a Titans Academy to train and mentor young heroes. Unfortunately, after just one school year, the Academy was destroyed by Deathstroke, who turned out to be possessed by the Great Darkness, a threat from Darkseid's planet of Apokolips. The Titans reformed as a premier team on a par with the Justice League.

guide.overview: Starfire is a powerful **defensive** Supporter who creates an energy field that grants **DMG reduction** and **healing over time** to all allies.

legacyPieces.name: Starfire's Starbolts
legacyPieces.reason: Starfire's signature gear. Increases her Attack when she casts her Ultimate and heals nearby allies, which is a rare source of healing from gear. Her Ultimate also boosts allies' Attack, while each cast stacks her own Attack, allowing Starfire to protect and empower the team simultaneously.

legacyPieces.name: Starheart Staff
legacyPieces.reason: Increases nearby allies' Attack and Physical and Spiritual Defense when Starfire casts her Ultimate. Since her Ultimate creates an energy field that provides damage reduction, this staff lets the squad gain damage reduction, Attack, Physical Defense, and Spiritual Defense bonuses all at once.

legacyPieces.name: Coluan Force Field Belt
legacyPieces.reason: Increases HP, Spiritual Defense, and Crit Resistance. Starfire stands at the center of her energy field to protect allies, so high survivability is crucial for keeping the field active consistently.

legacyPieces.name: Pied Piper Flute
legacyPieces.reason: Improves healing abilities. Starfire's energy field provides healing over time to allies within range, and the healing bonus strengthens her role as a versatile defensive Supporter.
